tldr: For the stated complete-curve, binary-strata causal cusp benchmark, the physical barycenter transport has a full-class uniform Gaussian-functional norm law and an asymptotically exact whole-tuple bootstrap confidence ball. Its squared-risk scale is \(D_n(\gamma)/n\), with a \(1/\log n\) exponent window and a critical logarithm. The observable horizontal Gaussian smoothing estimator has a uniform risk comparison in every window and attains exact local asymptotic minimax constants in the specified one-dimensional fixed subcritical and critical families; at the elbow the constant is \(k_P\sigma_0^2/2\) under \(n/\log n\) normalization. Legal bounded-score submodels give matching risk and honest-radius orders throughout. At interior laws the \(H\) information boundary is \(\gamma=1/2\), with canonical efficiency in separated regular regimes. Identification is inherited from Lin--Kong--Wang. Broader models containing the hard submodels inherit negative conclusions by subclass inclusion; positive uniform results remain confined to the benchmark.
gap: Aligned causal contrast limits erase the reference-coordinate residual. Smooth scalar transport bands assume positive target density. Jump-map norm bootstrap arguments do not control two moving continuous cusp compositions uniformly in a changing exponent.
fill: The benchmark retains the entire public curve-support class. A single two-map expansion supplies original and conditional norm limits; bounded-score causal submodels supply all-estimator order comparisons, and the regular branch identifies the canonical covariance.
